comments.note: In ThumbnailsViewModel.cs, the SelectAll/SelectNone commands call NotifyHasSelectionChanged() explicitly after the foreach loop. This is technically redundant since each item.IsSelected setter fires OnItemPropertyChanged which calls NotifyHasSelectionChanged(). The extra call is harmless (just fires a redundant PropertyChanged) but slightly misleading. Low priority — does not affect correctness.

ThumbnailsViewModel.Load() creates fire-and-forget bitmap loads via '_ = item.LoadBitmapAsync(_cts.Token)'. Unhandled exceptions from these tasks are silently swallowed. A try/catch in LoadBitmapAsync itself only catches CancellationToken throws — other IO exceptions from corrupt .thb2 files would be silently lost. Consider logging failures in LoadBitmapAsync, though this is out of scope for this WP.

comments.note: FakeThumbnailsRepository always returns an empty list from GetByMovieIdAsync, so there is no test that exercises LoadCommand with actual repository data. The Load code path is correct, but a test that configures the fake to return 2+ thumbnails and verifies they populate Thumbnails (and TabLabel updates) would improve confidence. Low priority — code is clearly correct by inspection.

DeleteSelectedCommand has CanExecute tests but no async-execution test that verifies repo.DeleteAsync is called, File.Delete is attempted, items are removed from Thumbnails, and item.Dispose() is invoked. Recommend adding an integration-style unit test using the fake repo to cover this path.

DeleteSelectedCommand iterates over a pre-captured 'selected' snapshot and deletes items sequentially. If a CancellationToken fires mid-loop, some items will be deleted from DB/disk/collection and others will not. This partial-delete state is non-critical for this use case but worth noting for future hardening.

Dispose_ClearsAllItems verifies the collection is emptied but does not verify that item.Dispose() was actually called on each ThumbnailItemViewModel or that _cts was cancelled. A spy/mock-based test would provide stronger guarantees on resource cleanup.

summary: ThumbnailsViewModel reviewed against all WP acceptance criteria, architecture conventions, and the four review dimensions. No blocking issues found.

Maintainability: Class is well-organized into clearly delineated regions (collection, computed properties, commands, lifecycle). All public members have XML docs. Constructor is unambiguous DI-only. Code is readable at a glance.

Best Practices: MVVM pattern followed correctly. CollectionChanged + PropertyChanged double-subscription pattern is correctly paired with explicit unsubscription in Load(), Dispose(), and the collection change handler. IsBusy gate on DeleteSelectedCommand.CanExecute is correctly declared via [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor] and checked in the CanExecute predicate. The Load-before-clear explicit manual unsubscription correctly handles the ObservableCollection Reset event limitation.

Performance: No bottlenecks. Fire-and-forget bitmap loads use instance _cts.Token (correct — loads persist past LoadCommand cancellation, stopped only by Dispose). DeleteSelected captures a snapshot before the loop (avoids enumeration-of-modified-collection issues).

Future Context: JumpToPosition stub is clean and non-intrusive. The linked CancellationTokenSource pattern in Load() is consistent with the established project pattern. api-surface.md already documents this class accurately. file-tree.md was updated by the Developer.

comments.note: SelectAll() and SelectNone() call NotifyHasSelectionChanged() explicitly after the foreach loop. This is redundant because each item.IsSelected setter fires OnItemPropertyChanged → NotifyHasSelectionChanged() already. The result is N+1 invocations for N items on every SelectAll/SelectNone call. Harmless and already noted by the Developer — no action required, but a comment explaining the intent (e.g. 'ensure final state is notified even if collection is empty') would improve readability.

FakeThumbnailsRepository.GetByMovieIdAsync always returns an empty list, leaving the LoadCommand's data-population path untested. A test that pre-configures the fake to return 2+ Thumbnail records and verifies Thumbnails.Count and TabLabel would improve confidence. Coverage gap is low-priority and code is correct by inspection.

No async execution test for DeleteSelectedCommand. The command's CanExecute path is tested but there is no test verifying that repo.DeleteAsync is called, File.Delete is attempted (or skipped when the file does not exist), items are removed from Thumbnails, and item.Dispose() is invoked. Recommend adding a unit test using the fake repo in a future iteration.
